**The Whispering Trees**

In a quiet corner of the world, where the sky meets the earth in a soft, blue haze, there stands a forest of ancient trees. They are not like ordinary trees—their bark is etched with silver veins that glow faintly under the moonlight, and their leaves shimmer like emeralds when the wind rustles through them.

The villagers nearby call them the Whispering Trees, for if you press your ear to their trunks, you can hear faint murmurs—voices from long ago, stories woven into the wood. Some say the trees remember everything: the laughter of children who once played beneath their branches, the tears of lovers who carved their names into the bark, the secrets of travelers who rested in their shade.

One evening, a young girl named Liora ventured into the forest, drawn by the tales her grandmother had told her. She placed her palm against the oldest tree, its trunk wide and gnarled with time. At first, she heard nothing. But then—a whisper.

*"Listen,"* the tree seemed to say.

And so she did.

The voice told her of a time when the forest was young, when the first humans had come with fire and fear, and how the trees had learned to speak to calm their hearts. It spoke of a great storm that had split the earth, and how the roots of the trees had held the land together. It spoke of a child, long ago, who had gotten lost in the woods and been guided home by the rustling leaves.

Liora stayed until the stars blinked awake, her heart full of stories. When she returned to the village, she carried a single silver leaf in her pocket—a gift from the Whispering Trees.

And from that day on, whenever someone asked her about the forest, she would smile and say, *"The trees remember. And if you listen closely, they might just tell you."*
